feed.title: Viatris sues Novo Nordisk over generic Wegovy patent dispute
feed.summary: Viatris has filed a lawsuit against Novo Nordisk in a Delaware federal court, seeking a ruling that its generic version of Wegovy would not infringe Novo Nordisk's patent. Novo Nordisk's patents covering semaglutide, the active ingredient in Wegovy and Ozempic, are set to expire in 2032.

feed.title: Delta Air Lines Stock Rises Friday: What's Going On?

This decline in fuel costs provides a significant operational benefit to airlines, especially heading into the holiday travel season, enhancing expected profitability for Delta.

feed.title: Why Berkshire Hathaway Sold Oil and Bought Delta Air Lines
feed.summary: Berkshire Hathaway, now run by Greg Abel, has significantly increased its stake in Delta Air Lines while reducing its position in Chevron, a move that contrasts with Warren Buffett's previous aversion to airline investments. This shift comes amidst high jet fuel prices, which have severely impacted the airline industry, yet Berkshire Hathaway appears to be betting on Delta's strategic advantages, such as owning its own refinery, to navigate the challenging market. The article suggests that while fuel costs remain a threat, the futures market anticipates some relief, and Delta is well-positioned among its peers.

feed.title: Canada's next rate move may be a hike, not a cut, says RBC
feed.summary: RBC economists predict that the Bank of Canada (BoC) is more likely to hike interest rates than cut them in the future, with a potential hiking cycle beginning in early 2027. This outlook is driven by factors such as the impact of US tariffs on Canadian imports and persistent inflation concerns from elevated global oil prices. For mortgage brokers, this suggests that the period of stable rates may be ending, requiring a shift in conversations with clients from an easing to a hiking rate cycle.

feed.title: Only 5 Hours: Inside Delta Air Lines' New Shortest Routes To Europe [Map]
feed.summary: Delta Air Lines offers several relatively short transatlantic routes to Europe, with the shortest being a seasonal service from JFK to Reykjavík at just five hours and 25 minutes. Other quick routes include seasonal flights to Iceland from Detroit and Minneapolis, and year-round services to Dublin, London, Edinburgh, and Lisbon from various US East Coast cities. These flights often leverage the geographic proximity of the US East Coast to Western Europe, enabling travel to new cultures in under six and a half hours.

feed.title: Top dividend aristocrats: Chevron, Emerson, and Albemarle lead on quality-adjusted fundamentals
feed.summary: Chevron Corp (CVX), Emerson Electric Company (EMR), and Albemarle Corp (ALB) have been identified as top dividend aristocrats based on quality-adjusted near-term fundamentals. These companies meet criteria including at least 25 years of dividend growth, positive projected EPS and revenue growth, dividend coverage above 1x, and a market capitalization over $10 billion. Chevron offers a strong balance of earnings momentum and dividend durability, Emerson boasts a clean operating-quality profile, and Albemarle shows significant near-term recovery potential.
